  January 27, 2021

ROLL CALL: At 6:04 p.m., on Wednesday, January 27, 2021 the Alhambra City Council met via
video conference.

COUNCIL PRESENT via video conference: LEE, MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER,
PÉREZ
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present physically, via teleconference, and via video conference: City Manager
Binnquist, City Attorney Montes, Assistant City Manager Garcia, City Clerk Myles, Director of
Community Development Castagnola, Deputy Director of Community Development Reynoso,
Principal Planner Lam

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M21-13

The City Clerk hereby reported that she duly gave notice of the special meeting of the City Council
being held this evening pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with Section 54956
of the Government Code of the State of California.

CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARING

1.  APPLICATIONS FOR VESTING TENTATIVE TRACT MAP TT 74194, RESIDENTIAL
  PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMIT RP-17-7, CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT CU-17-9
  AND DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE PROPOSED
  VILLAGES AT THE ALHAMBRA PROJECT (PROJECT) WITH 294 NEW, FOR-SALE,
  RESIDENTIAL DWELLING UNITS IN FIVE-STORY STACKED FLAT AND
  TOWNHOME CONFIGURATIONS; 545 NEW RENTAL APARTMENTS IN FIVE-STORY
  STACKED FLAT CONFIGURATIONS; AND UP TO 4,347 TOTAL PARKING SPACES
  TO ACCOMMODATE ALL NEW USES. IT IS EXPECTED THAT IF THE PROJECT IS
  APPROVED THE APPLICANT WILL IMPLEMENT A PARKING REDUCTION
  PURSUANT TO ALHAMBRA MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 23.52.060. THE PROJECT
  SITE IS LOCATED IN THE PO (PROFESSIONAL OFFICE) ZONE. AN
  ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT HAS BEEN PREPARED FOR THE PROJECT
  AND WILL ALSO BE CONSIDERED WITH THE PROJECT ALONG WITH A POSSIBLE
  STATEMENT OF OVERRIDING CONSIDERATIONS – F2M17-50, N2M20-163

  This was the time and place set by Notice No. N2M20-163 for the City Council to hold a
  public hearing, which public hearing was duly continued from the January 11, 2021
  meeting, to consider applications filed by ELITE-TRC Alhambra Community LLC, Elite-
  TRC North Parcel LLC; The Corner Company, LLC for Vesting Tentative Tract Map TT
  74194, Residential Planned Development Permit RP-17-7, Conditional Use Permit CU-
  17-9 and Development Agreement for the Development of the Proposed Villages at the
  Alhambra Project (Project). The Project covered portions of a 38.38-acre site bounded by

  1
1-27-21
   Fremont Avenue (west), Mission Road (south), Date Avenue (east), and Orange Street
  (north) in the City of Alhambra. The Project site was located in the PO (Professional Office)
  zone. The applicant requested approval of a Vesting Tentative Tract Map, Residential
  Planned Development Permit, Conditional Use Permit and Development Agreement for
  the development of the Project, as well as certification of an Environmental Impact Report
  (EIR) and adoption of a Statement of Overriding Considerations (SOC). If approved, the
  Project would retain 902,001 square feet of existing office space and would repurpose
  10,145 square feet of existing office space as Residential Amenity space. Also, the Project
  would retain a 50,000 square-foot LA Fitness health club, but would replace existing
  surface parking areas, warehouse/storage/maintenance buildings, and a vacant office
  building with a new multi-family residential development. The Project was originally
  submitted as a 1,061-unit development with 516 new, for-sale, residential dwelling units
  in five-story stacked flat and townhome configurations and 545 new rental apartments in
  five-story stacked flat configurations. Through the Planning Commission process, the
  Applicant modified the Project and reduced the number of proposed units to 839 (294
  for-sale, 545 rentals). Up to 4,347 new parking spaces would be provided to accommodate
  all of the uses, existing and new. The portions of the Project site slated for new
  development were designed in four Plan Areas: North Plan Area, East Plan Area, South
  Plan Area, and Corner Plan Area. The details of each Plan Area were discussed in further
  detail in the Residential Planned Development Section of this Analysis. The Project also
  proposed a reduction in the number of required parking spaces which is discussed in
  further detail in the Parking Section of this Analysis. It was the intent of the Applicant to
  develop the Project in phases. In furtherance of this, the Applicant proposed a
  Development Agreement for the Project.

  Between July 20, 2020 and November 16, 2020, the Planning Commission conducted
  nine (9) public hearings in considering the proposed The Villages at The Alhambra Project.
  At the September 21, 2020 Planning Commission meeting, the public comments portion
  of the public hearing closed with a total of 36 members of the public having spoken and
  339 written comments read into the record. At the October 5, 2020 Planning Commission
  meeting each of the Planning Commissioners were able to ask technical questions and
  express their thoughts and concerns. At the heart of the Planning Commission’s concerns
  were five issues pertaining to Project Density, Affordability/Inclusionary Housing,
  Community Benefits/Open Space, Traffic/Transportation, and Health/Site Contamination.
  At the November 2, 2020 Planning Commission meeting the Applicant returned to the
  Commission a Project with three (3) modifications: 1) The total number of units was
  reduced from 1,061 (516 for-sale, 545 rentals) to 839 (294 for-sale, 545 rentals); 2) The
  number of affordable housing units was increased from 55 units to 84 units; and 3) The
  Applicant decided to redesign the open space area in the North Plan Area to create a
  community park accessible to everyone, including the public. The Planning Commission
  was of the opinion these modifications were not sufficient and by a vote of 7-3, directed
  staff to return to the Commission at the November 16, 2020 meeting, with a Resolution
  recommending the City Council deny the proposed Project. At the November 16, 2020
  Planning Commission meeting, by a vote of 7-1, the Planning Commission adopted
  Resolution No. 20-20 recommending the City Council deny the proposed Project.

  On January 11, 2021, the City Council received staff presentation and the Applicant’s
  presentation on the proposed Project. There were 19 people waiting to speak on the Item,
  and 43 written comments that were to be read, however, due to the lateness of the hour
  and the City Council’s prior motion to end the meeting at 10:00 p.m., the public hearing
  was continued open to a special meeting of the City Council on Wednesday, January 27,

  2
1-27-21
   at 6:00 p.m. At tonight’s hearing, the City Council heard public testimony, and before or
  after the public testimony, staff requested Council provide direction concerning staff
  negotiating the proposed Development Agreement and/or City Council to designate a
  subcommittee for the purpose of negotiating the proposed Development Agreement. Also,
  time permitting, staff requested the City Council consider the merits of the Project.

  Discussion: Mayor PÉREZ acknowledged the high volume of public comment for the
  Public Hearing and asked for the consensus of the Council to end the meeting at a specific
  time and continue the Public Hearing open to another date. Council agreed to end the
  meeting at 10:00 p.m. and continue it as open to another date. City Attorney MONTES
  suggested that a Councilmember make a motion at 10:00pm to continue the public
  hearing.

  Discussion: Mayor PÉREZ noted the time as 10:00 p.m. and referred to Council’s
  previous discussion at the beginning of the item to continue the Public Hearing as open.
  Council agreed to a future special meeting to be held on February 4, 2021 and
  Councilmember LEE motioned to continue the public hearing as open to that date. Mr.
  MAZA seconded the motion.

  Action Taken:  City Council continued the public hearing open to a special meeting
  of the Alhambra City Council on February 4, 2021 at 6:00 p.m.

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE Seconded:  MAZA
